added_failures_note: both arms read in one format; head-gate.log reports no failures (4 passed) and base-gate.log reports the three test ids, so the reviewed run added no failing test

findings.text: follow-on: storing the memo under both the pre-read and post-read stamp (reckon/mcp_views.py:1566-1567) lets a later read whose stamp equals the post-read stamp hit `before in cached[0]` and be served a value computed at the pre-read state, so a pointer written during the aggregate is present in the stamp but absent from the value; the docstring at reckon/mcp_views.py:1552 claims the opposite ("a pointer written during this aggregate is seen then"), and the memo is module-global and keyed so this is reachable. It is bounded to the window before the next stamp change and does not hold the node.

follow-on: the test docstring claims "A pointer written during the aggregate is seen next read", but no assertion checks the late pointer appears in the second result; only len(loads)==1 (:207) and first==second (:208) are asserted, and first==second holds trivially because the second call is served the memo, so the documented freshness property is unguarded and, per the implementation, false.

follow-on: _default_cache_root re-implements the user-cache resolution (XDG_CACHE_HOME else ~/.cache, then /reckon) already owned by reckon/_store.py:193 cache_root, so the same base path now has two private spellings that can drift; the writability-fallback wrapper around it is new, so this is a partial duplication rather than a fully forked capability.

follow-on: the only recorded ruff log (/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261017T104516290345-a-fresh-read-takes-the-ledger-from-its-index/ruff.log) is red — EXIT=1 for both `ruff check` (PLW1510 here, W292 at :207) and `ruff format --check` — and predates the fix, while the manifest claims "test file 0"; the landed file at faee86b8e is in fact clean (verified: check EXIT=0, format EXIT=0), so the recorded ruff evidence is a stale pre-fix arm with no clean log recorded for the reviewed revision.
